track.name: excel-finance
track.label: Excel for Finance
track.summary: The Excel craft behind real financial work, from financial functions and model structure to three-statement, DCF and LBO builds, risk simulation and automation.

phases.title: Excel Foundations for Finance
phases.description: Set up Excel the way finance professionals run it: keyboard-only navigation, calculation options, and the number formats a model depends on.

phases.title: Financial Functions for Analysts
phases.description: The built-in functions every model leans on: time value of money, NPV/IRR and their irregular-cash-flow variants, depreciation, and date arithmetic.

phases.title: Lookup, Aggregation & Dynamic Array Formulas
phases.description: The formulas every model is actually built from: robust lookups, conditional sums, and the modern dynamic-array and LET/LAMBDA formulas that replace fragile legacy patterns.

phases.title: Business & Financial Modelling
phases.description: Structure assumptions, build a 3-statement model, and test it under different scenarios.

phases.title: Operating Model & Supporting Schedules
phases.description: The supporting schedules a 3-statement model is actually built on: a driver-based revenue and opex build, a working capital schedule, and a PP&E/capex roll-forward.

phases.title: Debt Schedules & Circularity
phases.description: Build a multi-tranche debt schedule with a revolver and cash sweep, then handle the circular reference that interest-on-average-debt always creates.

phases.title: DCF & Valuation Builds
phases.description: Discount a company's own projected cash flows to a value, then check that value against what the market pays for comparable companies.

phases.title: LBO & Merger Model Builds
phases.description: The two transaction models built on everything so far: a leveraged buyout returns model, and a merger model that tests whether a deal helps or hurts the acquirer's EPS.

phases.title: Monte Carlo Simulation in Excel
phases.description: Go beyond a single sensitivity table: simulate thousands of scenarios from input distributions and read the resulting range of outcomes.

phases.title: Finance Charts & Visualization
phases.description: The chart types finance actually uses in a deck or a board pack: a valuation range, a P&L bridge, and a budget-vs-actual variance view.

phases.title: Dashboards & Reporting Packs
phases.description: Turn a model's output into a one-page dashboard a manager can actually read, using the charts already built and a handful of interactive controls.

phases.title: VBA for Finance
phases.description: Automate the repetitive parts of the job: record and edit macros, loop through a workbook to build a report, and write your own custom functions.

phases.title: Power Query for Finance
phases.description: Stop rebuilding the same cleanup by hand every month: connect, clean and combine GL extracts, bank statements and multi-entity files with a query you can just refresh.

phases.title: Speed & Efficiency Drills
phases.description: Turn everything built so far into actual speed — the keyboard-only, no-mistakes pace a live modeling test or a real deadline demands.

phases.title: Modelling Tests & Case Studies
phases.description: The capstone: build under the same time pressure and ambiguity as a real modeling test, then check your work against a real answer key.

topics.title: Financial Modelling Fundamentals
topics.description: How a model is structured: inputs, calculations, and outputs kept separate, with the formatting and audit conventions that keep it trustworthy.

steps.d: Rebuild a messy sheet into three visually distinct blocks: blue hardcoded inputs, black calculations, and a clearly labelled output block.

steps.t: Apply the FAST colour and layout standard
steps.d: Colour every cell in a small model by the FAST convention (blue inputs, black formulas, green links, red external links) and check every formula in a row is identical.

steps.t: Add sign conventions and timing flags
steps.d: Decide a consistent sign convention for revenues vs costs and add a header flag row (e.g. historical/forecast switch) that other formulas reference.
Add a checks row that flags when a balance sheet doesn't balance or a percentage doesn't sum to 100%, and trace it to zero.
Use Trace Precedents/Dependents and the Watch Window to follow a value through a multi-tab model.

topics.title: Building a 3-Statement Model
topics.description: Link the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement into one model, and force the balance sheet to balance.

steps.d: Build a revenue build and an opex schedule that the income statement will pull from, on their own supporting tab.
Flow net income into retained earnings, capex/depreciation into PP&E, and the cash flow statement into the cash balance.

steps.t: Add and resolve the balance sheet check
steps.d: Add an assets-minus-liabilities-and-equity check row and trace any imbalance back to a broken link.

steps.t: Use a cash flow sweep or revolver plug
steps.d: Add a minimum cash balance and a revolver draw/paydown so the model self-balances under different scenarios.

topics.title: Scenario & Sensitivity Analysis
topics.description: Stress-test a model's assumptions with data tables, scenario switches, and Goal Seek instead of trusting a single forecast.

steps.t: Build a one- and two-variable data table
steps.d: Set up a data table that flexes revenue growth and margin together and shows the output grid.
Build a single scenario toggle cell that drives every assumption in the model via CHOOSE or IF.

steps.t: Run Goal Seek on a target output
steps.d: Use Goal Seek to find the growth rate that produces a target valuation or breakeven year.
Rank a model's assumptions by how much each one swings the output, and present that as a tornado chart.

topics.title: Keyboard-Only Navigation & Shortcuts
topics.description: Move around a workbook, select ranges, and switch sheets without ever touching the mouse — the baseline speed habit every finance role expects.

steps.d: Jump to the edge of a data block and extend a selection to it, on a real multi-tab workbook, without using the mouse.
Practice Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown between sheets and freeze panes so headers stay visible while you scroll.

steps.t: Print and keep a shortcut cheat sheet
steps.d: Download a finance-specific shortcut cheat sheet and keep it open for your first week of practice.

steps.t: Time yourself on a navigation drill
steps.d: Rebuild a small model's formatting and navigate its tabs entirely by keyboard, timing yourself against the mouse-driven version.

topics.title: Excel Options & Number Formats for Model Setup
topics.description: Configure calculation settings and number formats before you start building, so the model behaves predictably later.

steps.t: Freeze the header row and input column
steps.d: Freeze panes on a sample model so row/column labels stay visible while scrolling.
Find the Formulas options for automatic vs manual calculation and iterative calculation, and explain when each is used.
Write a custom format code that shows negative numbers in parentheses and hides zeros, and apply it to a sample column.

topics.title: Time Value of Money Functions
topics.description: PV, FV, PMT, RATE and NPER — the five functions behind every loan, annuity and savings calculation.

steps.t: Compute a present and future value
steps.d: Use PV and FV on a simple lump-sum investment and confirm the sign convention (cash out is negative).
Use PMT to compute the monthly payment on a loan, matching the rate and NPER units (monthly rate, monthly periods).
Use RATE and NPER to find the interest rate or number of periods implied by a known payment.

topics.title: NPV, IRR, XIRR & MIRR
topics.description: Discount a stream of cash flows and find its rate of return — and know when regular NPV/IRR are wrong.

steps.t: Discount periodic cash flows with NPV
steps.d: Build an NPV formula over evenly spaced annual cash flows and confirm it excludes the period-0 outflow.

steps.t: Switch to XNPV for irregular dates
steps.d: Rebuild the same cash flows with real calendar dates and XNPV, and compare the result to plain NPV.
Solve for the rate of return on the same two cash flow sets with IRR and XIRR and explain why they differ.

steps.t: Compute MIRR and explain when to use it
steps.d: Use MIRR with separate finance and reinvestment rates, and explain why it avoids IRR's multiple-solutions problem.

topics.title: Depreciation & Date Functions for Models
topics.description: Depreciate an asset three different ways and handle the date arithmetic that schedules and debt models depend on.

steps.d: Depreciate the same asset with SLN and DDB and chart the two depreciation curves side by side.

steps.t: Use EDATE and EOMONTH for period ends
steps.d: Generate a run of month-end and anniversary dates for a schedule using EDATE and EOMONTH.
Calculate a settlement or due date that skips weekends using WORKDAY.

topics.title: Lookup Formulas: INDEX/MATCH, XLOOKUP & Why to Avoid OFFSET/INDIRECT
topics.description: Robust ways to pull a value from a table, and why OFFSET and INDIRECT are a modelling liability even though they can do the same job.

steps.d: Replace a VLOOKUP with INDEX/MATCH on a table where the lookup column isn't the leftmost one.
Rewrite the same lookup with XLOOKUP and compare readability and its built-in 'not found' handling.
Find any OFFSET or INDIRECT formulas in a sample workbook and explain what precedent they hide from the dependency tree.
Rewrite an OFFSET-based dynamic range using INDEX instead, and confirm the output is identical.

topics.title: SUMIFS, SUMPRODUCT & Conditional Aggregation
topics.description: Summing and counting by condition — the two workhorse functions behind every summary schedule and check row.

steps.d: Use SUMIFS to total a transaction list by both account and month in one formula.

steps.t: Use SUMPRODUCT for weighted and array math
steps.d: Use SUMPRODUCT to compute a weighted average or a conditional count that SUMIFS can't express directly.
Pair COUNTIFS and AVERAGEIFS with the same criteria pattern to check your SUMIFS total against a count and an average.

topics.title: Dynamic Arrays, LET & LAMBDA
topics.description: Modern Excel 365 formulas that spill results across a range and let you name and reuse logic inside a single formula.

steps.d: Write a formula that returns a multi-cell array and watch it spill into neighboring cells without Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

steps.t: Simplify a nested formula with LET
steps.d: Take a formula that repeats the same sub-calculation twice and rewrite it with LET so it's computed once and named.
Open a workbook with a named LAMBDA function in the Name Manager and trace how it's called like a native function.

topics.title: Revenue & Opex Build
topics.description: Forecast the top of the income statement from explicit business drivers instead of a hardcoded growth rate.

steps.d: Build an assumptions block with volume, price and mix drivers that the revenue formula references — never hardcode growth into the formula itself.
Project each opex line as a percent of revenue or headcount driver, on its own supporting tab.

steps.t: Flow the build into the income statement
steps.d: Link the revenue and opex build into a summarized income statement tab.

topics.title: Working Capital Schedule
topics.description: Forecast operating assets and liabilities as a percent of sales or COGS, and turn that into the change in NWC the cash flow statement needs.

steps.d: List non-cash current assets and non-debt current liabilities in balance-sheet order on a dedicated schedule.
Calculate days sales outstanding, days inventory and days payable outstanding from historical data.

steps.t: Project and link to the cash flow statement
steps.d: Forecast each line from its ratio, calculate the period-over-period change in NWC, and link it into the cash flow statement.

topics.title: PP&E / Capex & Depreciation Schedule
topics.description: Roll forward gross PP&E, accumulated depreciation and net PP&E so capex, depreciation and the balance sheet all reconcile.

steps.d: Set up opening balance + capex − depreciation − disposals = closing balance for both gross and net PP&E.
Depreciate each year's capex on its own useful-life schedule so the total depreciation line reflects multiple overlapping asset vintages.

steps.t: Reconcile to the other two statements
steps.d: Confirm capex appears in investing cash flow, depreciation in the income statement, and net PP&E on the balance sheet all agree.

topics.title: Building a Debt Schedule
topics.description: Track each tranche of debt — beginning balance, draws, repayments, interest, ending balance — across every forecast period.

steps.d: Order the debt schedule revolver-first, then term loans, then subordinated debt, matching repayment priority.
For one tranche, set up beginning balance, draws, scheduled and optional repayments, and ending balance columns.
Sweep excess free cash flow into an optional prepayment on the most senior tranche and confirm it reduces next period's interest.

topics.title: Circular References, Circuit Breakers & Iterative Calculation
topics.description: Interest calculated on an average or ending debt balance feeds back into the cash flow that determines that same balance — handle the resulting circularity deliberately, not by accident.

steps.d: Build interest expense off an average debt balance and watch Excel flag the circular reference.
Enable iterative calculation with a sensible iteration/change limit so the loop resolves instead of erroring.
Add an IF-based toggle cell that zeroes out the circular interest calculation on command, so a bad input can't lock up the model.

topics.title: Discounted Cash Flow Model
topics.description: Project unlevered free cash flow, discount it at WACC, and add a terminal value to get an intrinsic enterprise value.

steps.d: Calculate UFCF as EBIT*(1-tax) + D&A +/- change in working capital − capex for each forecast year.
Compute WACC from the cost of equity, after-tax cost of debt, and the target capital structure weights.
Discount each year's UFCF to present value at WACC, then add a terminal value from the Gordon growth or exit multiple method.
Build a WACC-vs-terminal-growth data table around the resulting enterprise value.

topics.title: Trading & Transaction Comps Table
topics.description: Value a company against what the market actually pays for similar businesses, using a clean, formula-driven comps table.

steps.t: Select and lay out a peer set
steps.d: Pick a peer group and lay out a comps table with market cap, enterprise value, and the metrics each multiple needs.
Build the standard trading multiples for each peer and check for outliers before including them in a summary statistic.
Calculate the mean, median and quartile range across peers and apply it to the target's own metrics to get an implied value range.

topics.title: LBO Model From Scratch
topics.description: Fund an acquisition mostly with debt, run the target's cash flow through a debt paydown, and solve for the sponsor's return at exit.

steps.d: Lay out uses (purchase price, fees) against sources (debt tranches, sponsor equity) and confirm they balance.

steps.t: Project the target's standalone cash flow
steps.d: Forecast revenue, EBITDA and free cash flow for the target over the hold period.

steps.t: Run the debt paydown and exit
steps.d: Sweep free cash flow against the debt schedule, assume an exit multiple, and back out the equity value at exit.
Calculate the sponsor's IRR and multiple of invested capital from the entry equity check and the exit equity value.

topics.title: Merger Model & Accretion/Dilution Analysis
topics.description: Combine an acquirer and target's financials, layer in the deal's financing, and test whether the combined EPS beats the acquirer's standalone EPS.

steps.d: Set the offer price, premium, and the cash/stock/debt mix used to finance the deal.
Combine acquirer and target pre-tax income, then adjust for foregone interest on cash and new interest expense on deal debt.
Compute pro forma net income and diluted share count, then compare pro forma EPS to the acquirer's standalone EPS.
Flex the purchase price and financing mix in a data table and see which combinations turn the deal dilutive.

topics.title: Monte Carlo Fundamentals: RAND, NORM.INV & Distributions
topics.description: Turn a single-point forecast into a probability distribution using nothing but built-in Excel functions.

steps.d: Use RAND() to generate a random input between a low and high bound.
Use NORM.INV(RAND(), mean, stdev) to shape a random draw into a realistic normal distribution for a growth-rate assumption.

steps.t: Wire the draws into a live output
steps.d: Feed several randomized assumptions into your model's key output cell (e.g. NPV) so it recalculates with each draw.

topics.title: Data-Table-Driven Simulation & Tornado Charts
topics.description: Repeat a randomized model thousands of times without an add-in, and rank which assumption actually drives the spread of outcomes.

steps.t: Build a one-variable data table simulation
steps.d: Use a blank column feeding a one-variable data table to force Excel to recalculate the model hundreds of times and capture each output.
Chart a histogram of the simulated outputs and compute the mean, percentiles and probability of a negative outcome.

steps.t: Rank drivers with a tornado chart
steps.d: Build a tornado chart that ranks each input by how much it swings the output, from a stacked bar chart base.

topics.title: Football Field & Valuation Range Charts
topics.description: Show several valuation methodologies' low-high ranges on one chart, the way a banker's fairness-opinion deck does.

steps.d: Build a table of methodology, low value, high value and bar length (high minus low) for each valuation method.
Create a stacked bar chart with an invisible 'low' series and a visible 'range' series to make the bars float.
Add data labels, a current share price line, and clean up colors so it reads at a glance.

topics.title: Waterfall / Bridge Charts
topics.description: Show how a starting number is bridged to an ending number through a series of positive and negative steps.

steps.d: Use Excel's built-in Waterfall chart type on a simple revenue-to-net-income bridge.
Set the first, last and any subtotal bars as totals so they anchor to the baseline instead of floating.

steps.t: Build an EBITDA or budget bridge
steps.d: Rebuild the chart for a prior-year-to-current-year EBITDA bridge, labelling each driver of the change.

topics.title: Variance Charts (Actual vs Budget)
topics.description: Make a budget-vs-actual gap visible at a glance instead of buried in a table of numbers.

steps.d: Chart budget and actual side by side for each line item on a clustered column chart.
Build a second chart showing just the variance, colored by over/under budget, for a cleaner executive view.
Use conditional formatting or data labels to call out the line items with the largest variance.

topics.title: Finance Dashboard Design Principles
topics.description: The layout and formatting choices that make a dashboard readable in thirty seconds instead of five minutes.

steps.t: Separate data, calculation and dashboard tabs
steps.d: Split a report into three tabs — raw data, calculations, and the dashboard itself — so the dashboard tab only ever displays, never calculates.
Pick the 4-6 numbers that matter most and give them visual priority over everything else on the page.
Align numbers right and text left, add subtle row banding, and remove gridlines and chart junk.

topics.title: Building an Excel Finance Dashboard
topics.description: Wire slicers and dynamic titles into a dashboard so one control updates every chart and KPI on the page at once.

steps.d: Build each chart and KPI card off its own PivotTable so the whole dashboard stays dynamic as data updates.

steps.t: Connect a slicer to every chart
steps.d: Add a slicer and report-connect it to every PivotTable and PivotChart on the dashboard.
Build a formula-driven chart title that updates automatically to reflect the current slicer selection.

topics.title: VBA Fundamentals for Analysts
topics.description: Record your first macro, then read and edit the code it generates in the Visual Basic Editor.

steps.d: Turn on the macro recorder, format a range, stop recording, and run the macro on a fresh sheet.
Open the Visual Basic Editor and step through the recorded code line by line to see what each statement did.
Rewrite part of the recorded macro using a declared variable instead of a hardcoded cell reference.

topics.title: Loops, Automation & Report Generation
topics.description: Repeat an action across a range, a collection of sheets, or a folder of files instead of doing it by hand.

steps.d: Loop through a fixed number of rows and apply a calculation or formatting rule to each.
Loop through every worksheet in a workbook and export each one as its own PDF.
Chain loops and formatting into one macro that rebuilds a monthly report from a fresh data dump.

topics.title: User-Defined Functions (UDFs) for Finance
topics.description: Write your own worksheet function in VBA when nothing built into Excel does the calculation you need.

steps.d: Write a Function procedure in a standard module that takes two arguments and returns a value, then call it from a cell like any native function.
Write a UDF that replicates a multi-step calculation (e.g. a blended discount rate) your model currently spreads across several helper cells.
Explain why a UDF can't change other cells or formatting, and when a Sub is the right tool instead.

topics.title: Power Query Fundamentals for Finance Data
topics.description: Connect, transform and load data through Power Query's editor instead of formulas or copy-paste.

steps.d: Import a CSV or Excel export through Get & Transform and open it in the Power Query editor.
Remove columns, change data types and filter rows, then look at the applied-steps list and reorder one step to see the effect.
Load the query into a table, replace the source file, and click Refresh to confirm the same steps reapply automatically.

topics.title: Cleaning & Combining GL Extracts and Bank Statements
topics.description: Turn a messy general ledger or bank export into a clean, analysis-ready table every time it refreshes.

steps.d: Set correct data types, trim whitespace, and remove header/subtotal rows a GL export brought along.
Split a combined description column by delimiter and unpivot a wide GL export into a proper transaction table.

steps.t: Match a bank statement to the ledger
steps.d: Merge the bank statement and GL queries on date and rounded amount to flag unmatched transactions.

topics.title: Multi-Entity / Multi-File Consolidations
topics.description: Combine a folder of identically structured entity or period files into one consolidated table that updates itself.

steps.d: Point a query at a folder of monthly or per-entity files and combine them into a single appended table.
Handle a folder where one file has an extra column or different header row, and normalize it in the query.
Drop a new period's file into the folder and confirm Refresh All picks it up without touching the query.

topics.title: Timed Modelling Speed Drills
topics.description: Deliberate, timed repetition — not more new material — is what actually makes shortcuts and formulas automatic.

steps.d: Complete a timed keyboard-shortcut drill and note your time and error count.

steps.t: Rebuild a model from scratch, timed
steps.d: Set a 30-45 minute timer and rebuild a small model you've already built once, using only the keyboard.
Repeat the same drill weekly and track whether your time and error count are actually improving.

topics.title: Practice Case Studies & Modelling Tests
topics.description: Everything from this track, applied under a clock, against a case study you haven't seen before.

steps.d: Take a real company's filings and build a clean 3-statement model in a fixed time window, keyboard-only.
Complete a timed LBO modeling test from a blank workbook, then check sources & uses and the returns calculation against the answer key.
After each timed build, compare your file to the solution and write down the two or three mistakes that cost you the most time.
